headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but non-zero due to shared file and network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and ingest stdin/stdout, while Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled text from one system can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows ingest Plane-exported files or notes as task content
IF Plane users upload Kestra-generated artifacts and later copy them into automation inputs
mitigations: Restrict file exchange to a reviewed folder
Strip executable-looking directives from imported text
Use a one-way export format with schema validation
Add a manual approval step before any workflow execution
requires-engineering: implement provenance tagging across both systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, and has broad network egress; Plane touches files, images, hyperlinks, and notes. If the pair shares a workspace or file handoff, sensitive data can move from Kestra into Plane outputs or uploads. This is not proven by direct evidence, but the documented surfaces make leakage plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared directory or upload bucket
IF Kestra workflows forward logs or artifacts into Plane issue attachments
mitigations: Separate workspaces and storage buckets
Disable automatic attachment of logs and artifacts
Redact secrets before export
Limit Plane uploads to approved file types
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on all handoffs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has write_filesystem, execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, and broad network egress; Plane lacks filesystem write but still has broad egress and file uploads. Kestra also requests root and docker.sock, so if both are deployed against the same mutable resources, Kestra can overwrite or race with Plane-managed files or services. The blast radius can be irreversible, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable directory or deployment volume
IF Kestra is granted root or docker.sock in the same host namespace as Plane
mitigations: Run each agent in separate containers or VMs
Mount shared paths read-only
Remove docker.sock and root grants
Use distinct service accounts and storage paths
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra produces workflow outputs, logs, and artifacts that Plane can ingest as files, notes, or hyperlinks. Plane is an issue/task system, so if it treats Kestra output as authoritative, bad facts can cascade into incorrect tickets or scheduling actions. Because the handoff is a default-available integration pattern rather than a verified safeguard, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Plane tickets are auto-created from Kestra artifacts or logs
IF operators rely on Kestra output without a verification step before Plane actioning
mitigations: Require human review before ticket creation
Attach source links alongside every imported artifact
Validate Kestra outputs against a schema
Mark generated content as untrusted in Plane
requires-engineering: add checksum-based verification between systems

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. The only concrete compliance concern is that Kestra handles logs, database data, and cloud storage data while Plane handles files and notes, so a mismatch could arise if the operator routes regulated data through both. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow, not a single-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from Kestra into Plane without a retention policy review
IF the deployment requires residency or certification guarantees not documented in either profile
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Document retention for both systems
Separate EU and US data paths
Review export/delete behavior before rollout
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations
